sections.title: Teaching about Divorce
observations: In this section, Jesus addresses the topic of divorce, emphasizing the sanctity of marriage as a divine institution. He refers back to the creation narrative, highlighting that marriage is intended to be a lifelong commitment between a man and a woman.

The Pharisees question Jesus about the legality of divorce, attempting to trap Him in a debate over the Mosaic law. Jesus responds by pointing out that Moses allowed divorce due to the hardness of people's hearts, but it was not God's original intention.
This teaching challenges cultural norms and emphasizes the importance of faithfulness in marriage, calling believers to a higher standard of love and commitment.

sections.title: Jesus Blesses Little Children
observations: In this passage, people bring children to Jesus for Him to bless them. The disciples, however, rebuke the parents, thinking that Jesus is too important for such matters.

Jesus responds with indignation, stating that the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these. This highlights the value of childlike faith and the importance of welcoming children in the community of believers.
This section serves as a reminder of the inclusivity of Jesus' ministry and His love for the vulnerable and innocent.

sections.title: The Rich Young Ruler
observations: A young man approaches Jesus, seeking eternal life. Jesus tells him to keep the commandments, to which the young man confidently claims he has done since his youth.

Jesus then challenges him to sell his possessions and give to the poor, revealing the man's attachment to wealth. This interaction illustrates the difficulty of prioritizing spiritual wealth over material wealth.

Jesus concludes by teaching that it is hard for the rich to enter the kingdom of heaven, prompting His disciples to question who can be saved. Jesus reassures them that with God, all things are possible.

importantVerses.commentary: What therefore God has joined together, let not man separate. This verse underscores the divine nature of marriage and the seriousness of divorce.
But Jesus looked at them and said, 'With man this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.' This verse emphasizes God's power to save and transform lives, regardless of human limitations.

questions: What does Jesus' teaching on divorce reveal about God's design for marriage?
How can we apply Jesus' message about welcoming children in our churches today?
What does the interaction with the rich young ruler teach us about the relationship between wealth and discipleship?
